# Run ledger - P25.10 (contradiction serve-path: bounded latency over an append-only spine)

## Spec / Base / Branch / Config

- **Spec:** `docs/tickets/P25.10__contradiction-serve-path.md` (P25+ backlog,
  semantic id `API-PERF.1`)
- **Branch:** `devin/p25-10-contradiction-serve-path` - stacked on
  `devin/p25-9-meta-closures` (PR #91).
- **Date:** 2026-09-16. Hosted spine read via the Cloud SQL proxy
  (`127.0.0.1:5433` → `sig-pg`); the PG password rode env only
  (`gcloud secrets … sig-pg-password` → `$SIG_PG_PASSWORD`), never a file.

## Profiling finding (deliverable 1 - recorded before choosing the fix)

`/v1/contradiction` → `PgReadStore.contradictions()` → `_compute_on_read()`
iterated every public `(subject_id, predicate_id)` pair and called
`claims_for(pair)` per pair - **two round-trips per pair** (`_resolve_entity`
PK lookup + the claims SELECT with its `LATERAL` evidence join). Measured over
the live spine through the proxy (2026-09-16, 19,702 claims / 6,573 subjects /
**17,950 public pairs**):

| component | measured |
|---|---|
| `_claim_pairs` (pair enumeration) | 0.49 s |
| `claims_for` per pair (2 round-trips) | **92.7 ms/pair** → ~1,512 s projected locally (~105 s hosted, Cloud SQL latency is lower) |
| one set-based fetch of all 19,702 public claims | **3.07 s** |
| `RESOLVE` over all 17,950 in-memory groups | **0.10 s** → 1 contradiction, 12,918 KeyErrors (the 67 unregistered live predicates from the P25.9 calibration note) |

The bottleneck was the per-pair read loop - a classic N+1 - not the resolver.
Per the ticket's ordering, the fix pushes the set-based work into SQL FIRST,
then caches the result against the spine watermark.

## What landed (deliverable 2 - the serve-path fix)

`api/src/api/store_pg.py`:

- **`_public_claim_groups(conn, belief)`** - one set-based SELECT over the whole
  spine (the same SELECT `claims_for` issues per pair: `sensitivity_tier = 0`
  publication boundary + `sys_period @> belief` as-of predicate + the `LATERAL`
  evidence join), grouped in memory by `(subject_id, predicate_id)`.
  `claim.subject_id` IS the entity id, so no per-pair entity resolution is
  needed - the resolver receives byte-identical `Claim` groups.
- **`_spine_watermark()`** - a monotone key over the append-only spine:
  `count(claim)`, `count(claim WHERE upper(sys_period) IS NOT NULL)` (the one
  permitted mutation - closing `sys_period` - is counted, so even it bumps the
  key), `max(lower(sys_period))` (latest assertion instant), and the row counts
  of the other three tables the compute reads (`claim_evidence`,
  `evidence_capture`, `evidence_artifact`). Append-only ⇒ any write that could
  change the served set changes the key: **provably never stale**, no TTL.
- **`_annotation_view()`** - persisted `graph_annotations` rows stay
  authoritative and are read live; the compute-on-read fallback is memoised per
  instance against the watermark under `threading.Lock` (at most one compute per
  instance per watermark, even under concurrent requests). The watermark is read
  BEFORE the data so the disclosed state never overstates freshness. The compute
  runs on a dedicated connection (`_connect`, same `SET ROLE`) so a multi-second
  compute cannot interleave statements with per-request reads on `_conn`.
- **`annotation_watermark()`** - the watermark the last-served set was computed
  at (the cache key, not a fresh read - no recompute race in the route).
- **`warmup()`** - a daemon thread runs the view at startup so even the first
  user request is warm; wired in `sig-api serve` (`cli.py`), no-op for the demo
  store.

`api/src/api/models.py` + `routes.py`: `spine_watermark: str | None` added to
`ContradictionCollection`, `ContradictionResponse`, `TaskCollection`,
`TaskResponse` (additive, back-compatible) - a cached answer states which spine
state it describes (§3.1 freshness disclosed, not implied). `ReadStore` gains
`annotation_watermark()` + `warmup()`; `InMemoryStore` returns `None`/no-ops.

**Same-shape endpoint check (deliverable 4):** `/v1/task` shared the identical
compute-on-read pass - now served from the same cached view (0.18 s hosted).
`/v1/search`/`dossier`/`coverage` are different, bounded shapes (per-matched-
entity lookups, `LIMIT`-bounded), not the whole-spine pass - recorded, not
scope-creeped. No derived/precomputed sqitch store was needed: the set-based
compute is ~1 s, so no new schema change.

## Prove invalidation (deliverable 3 - deterministic test)

`tests/api/test_store_pg.py::test_watermark_keyed_serve_path_discloses_and_invalidates`
(Docker-gated, real PG18+PostGIS + sqitch plan):

- first GET serves the seeded 299-vs-190 contradiction with `spine_watermark`
  disclosed at collection and item level;
- second GET at the same watermark: identical set, `compute_calls == 1`
  (spy on `_compute_on_read`) - no recompute;
- `PgClaimSink.assert_claims` lands a new 11-vs-22 `claimed_device_count` pair
  on a fresh subject → next GET: **watermark changed**, exactly one new
  contradiction alongside the old one, `compute_calls == 2` - the cache can
  never serve a stale set;
- `/v1/task` shares the same view and disclosure;
- `tests/api/test_api_units.py` pins `spine_watermark: null` for the seeded
  in-memory store.

`SIG_REQUIRE_DB_TESTS=1 uv run pytest tests/api/test_store_pg.py` - 4/4 passed
(real testcontainer run, not a skip).

## Hosted timing (deliverable - live verification)

`curl -w '%{time_total}'` against `https://sig-api-e5ctyx36jq-uc.a.run.app`:

| when | time |
|---|---|
| **before** (revision sig-api-00001) | **113.6 s** then **131.5 s** - every request recomputed |
| **after** (revision `sig-api-00002-b55`, image `sig-api:latest` rebuilt from this branch) | **cold 1.01 s** (startup warmup already ran), warm **0.17 / 0.17 / 0.17 / 0.24 s** |

Warm p95 ≈ 0.24 s - the < 5 s target is met with ~20x headroom. The served set
is byte-identical to the pre-fix response (same `contradiction_id`, same
`claim_ids`); `spine_watermark` =
`claims=19702 closed=0 latest_assertion=2026-09-16T17:41:14.323227+00:00 evidence=19702/23/23`.

  2 skipped**, verify-gen clean.
- Invariants kept: spine insert-only (no writes added; the fix is reads plus an
  in-process memo - no sqitch change needed), RLS/`SET ROLE` untouched (the
  compute connection applies the same role), reads read-only, contradictions
  stay visible, freshness disclosed.
- No secret literal anywhere; credentials stayed env-only.
